mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% while PAYEMS increases by at least 2% in the same month
failure_condition: In a sample of 20 triggered events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a sustained rise in home sales (HOUST) indicates expanding manufacturing and consumer demand, which elevates equity risk premiums and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by > 3% in a month and HOUST increases by > 2% in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the signal (Rank IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months suggests deflationary pressure, lowering real discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the US Treasury yield on 10-year bonds (implied by market rates) rises by more than 10 bps over the next month, it reflects higher real rates that discount future equities, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: 10Y Treasury yield increases by > 10 bps in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with the yield increase (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate below 3.5% followed by a sustained increase in job openings (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market, which can lead to wage growth and inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS increases by > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (HOUST) without a corresponding decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggest strong consumer demand that outpaces manufacturing, which can overheat the economy and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% while INDPRO remains flat or decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative in 70% of triggered events (chi-squared p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months) and rising discount rates (FEDFUNDS > 4%), the real present value of future equities declines, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when the trigger is met.
